▪︎prognosis poor: 90% die of the dz; outcomes depend on stage @ dx
▪︎~37% of US adults currently or formerly smoke
LABS: hypercalcemia (PTHrP or bone METS), hyponatremia (SIADH), exudative effusion
▪︎RF: also 2nd-hand smoke, diesel fuels, ionizing radiation, metals (arsenic, chromium, nickel, iron oxide), industrial carcinogens; COPD, sarcoidosis
▪︎S/SXS: also anorexia, asthenia, chest/rib/vertebral/pelvic pain from METS; hoarseness (recurrent laryngeal n. compression)
▪︎Adenocarcinoma: arises from mucous glands or epithelial cells w.in/distal to the terminal bronchioles → periph nodules or masses
▪︎Lrg cell: undifferentiated, aggressive, rapid doubling times
▪︎SCLC: infiltrates submucosally → bronchial narrowing w/o a discrete mass
▪︎Squamous: arises from bronchial epithelium; discrete intraluminal mass

TTF-1, napsin A, CK 7, mucicarmine, PAS-D
▪︎CXR cannot r/o lung CA if suspected → CT chest w/ contrast
▪︎BX (CT-guided needle aspiration, bronchoscopy, or thoracentesis) → type of lung CA + guides TX
▪︎contrast-enhanced CT chest = most important radiologic study for dx + initial staging
▪︎tx depends on staging; also immunotherapy, TKIs if ⊕ALK or EGFR mutations
▪︎NSCLC: surgical resection = tx of choice for limited, nonmetastatic dz; radiation may be an adjunct to surg
▪︎SCLC: limited → radiation + chemo; extensive → chemo alone; surg = limited utility
▪︎who to screen: consider age, amt of smoke exposure, time since quitting
▪︎d/c screening once ⍉smoked x15yrs or a health problem limits life expectancy; pt must be willing to undergo tx (incl lung surg)
▪︎smoke cessation counseling for all pts who smoke; screening participation assoc w/ ⇡ quit rates
